text:
Tampa Bay's season has a question hanging over it that no win streak answers. Nikita Kucherov told the Lightning at the end of October that he won't re-sign and asked for a trade, according to the Associated Press, and general manager Julien BriseBois has said he has no intention of moving him. In the meantime Kucherov keeps producing, and Buffalo knows it better than anyone: he has 12 points in his last five games against the Sabres, and the Lightning beat them 8-3 in Buffalo on Nov 11.

That score flattered Tampa. Our replays gave the Lightning that game only 52% of the time, and the same theme runs through Buffalo's whole season. The Sabres are 13 goals underwater on a chance gap of just 3.2, with finishing (6.0 goals short of what their shots usually produce) and goaltending (3.9 goals allowed above expected) doing the damage. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen gets the net one win from 100 for his career, but at .872 and 1.8 goals below expected in 13 games, after saving 9.1 above expected last season. Alex Lyon, as Bleacher Report's Joe Yerdon noted, is still looking for his first win.

The trip has been long. This is the last stop of six on the road (1-3-1 so far), and the second night of a back-to-back after Sam Bennett's hat trick beat them 4-3 in Sunrise. Tage Thompson has goals in three straight, including a 90.7 mph equalizer last night, and Jack Quinn is in the middle of a breakout. Buffalo also takes 4.1 penalties a game, and Tampa's power play doesn't need the help.

The Lightning are without Brandon Hagel (24 points in 20 games). Jake Guentzel has slid into his spot beside Anthony Cirelli and Kucherov, and John Carlson has 14 points in his last ten. Our numbers have Tampa at 3.69 expected goals and Buffalo at 2.67. The Sabres' playoff chances sit at 17% in our simulations, Tampa's at 97%.
headline: Sabres finish a long trip against Kucherov's Lightning
